prompt:
A full-body character image, vertical 2:3 (1024×1536): Lü Bu of the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, reimagined as an adult woman — the mightiest warrior under heaven, rider of Red Hare.

1. STYLE
Korean MMORPG character artwork. A recognisably drawn face with gently simplified anatomical structure. 2D painting with visible brushwork: layered strokes of colour, soft broken edges, thin coloured linework and a few crisp accents on the face and costume.
Her face is small and soft: a short midface, a softly rounded jaw and a small chin, about 1.3 times as long as it is wide, with her eyes open at their natural size. Bangs, side locks and headpieces frame the face without lengthening it.
Skin finish: dewy, glass-like highlights on the skin of her shoulders, arms, collarbones and legs — a soft, luminous wet-look sheen that follows the body's forms; her face keeps a soft, natural finish.

2. CHARACTER
Age: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face.
Face — her own, recognisably this character, a woman's face with no beard or facial hair: a fierce, wild ferocity; light warm-beige skin with a golden undertone; diamond-shaped face; medium-sized eyes — narrow upturned eyes, outer eye corners slightly lifted; sharp angled brows; aquiline nose; full wide lips; crimson eyes; sharp winged eyeliner.
Body and hair: tall and statuesque with long legs and a full, curvaceous figure — full bust and hips, narrow waist build; long wavy hair with long bangs falling over one eye; plum-black hair with a violet sheen.
Expression: a faint knowing smile, subtle and relaxed.
Legend, carried in her design and bearing: unmatched might — the greatest warrior under heaven, two long pheasant-tail plumes rising from her headpiece, a red-and-black war cape, proud and capricious, betrayal after betrayal.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME AND EQUIPMENT — THREE KINGDOMS
Costume: Three Kingdoms war general's armor — lamellar scale armor laced over a silk battle robe, beast-head shoulder guards, a plumed helmet or a war headband, a long war cape, her weapon at hand. Late-Han Chinese dress — cross-collared silk robes with wide sleeves and a broad sash, lamellar or scale armor laced with cords where armor is worn, bronze, jade and lacquer ornament, Han court hair ornaments; silk, lacquered leather, bronze and iron.
Silhouette: layered laced lamellar armor, big heavy beast-head pauldrons and armored skirts to the knees — a broad, weighty general's silhouette. This silhouette sets the overall shape of the costume above — keep its materials, ornaments and rank in this shape; the details are free.
Colours: scarlet red, black lacquer, burnished gold and white plume accents.
Signature item: the Sky Piercer, a crescent-bladed fangtian ji halberd. She holds it at full scale: one whole object, drawn once, held in front of or beside her body; a long weapon keeps one straight, unbroken shaft with a single head or blade.
Exposure (bold): her robes open to show skin — the cross collar opened into a deep neckline with natural cleavage, bare upper arms above detached wide sleeves (and bare shoulders where no shoulder guard sits), a high slit in the skirt panels showing the thigh; any armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Intimate areas covered; keep the costume material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: the chaos of the late Eastern Han, around 184–200 AD: burning Luoyang, the Hulao Pass, Yellow Turban fields, warlord camps of rival banners, frontier steppe and the southern jungles of the Nanman.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: a soft key light with a strong rim light tracing her hair, shoulders and armour; bright, crisp specular highlights on metal and jewellery, and a clean, warm-neutral sheen on her skin.
Composition: her whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet inside the frame with clear margins, about four-fifths of the image height; camera at chest height with natural portrait perspective.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only — no second character, horse or other creature. No readable text or numbers, except that a banner, seal or emblem may carry the single character 雄 or 呂. No logo, watermark, speech bubble or frame border. Three Kingdoms-era Chinese dress, architecture and materials only.
Avoid: a blue or bruise-like tint on the skin around the eyes, glossy or shiny highlights on the face, sweaty, oily or plastic-looking skin.

observations: Single woman, whole body with two arms and two legs, both hands visible.
Weapon or plume tips touch frame edges; retained as required.
